column1: Japan has a significantly better record in terms of average mathematical attainment than England and Wales.
column2: 就学生的平均数学成绩而言，日本的表现明显优于英格兰和威尔士。

column1: Large sample international comparisons of pupils’ attainments since the 1960s have established that not only did Japanese pupils at age 13 have better scores of average attainment, but there was also a larger proportion of ‘low’ attainers in England, where, incidentally, the variation in attainment scores was much greater.
column2: 自20世纪60年代以来，对各国学生学业成绩所作的大样本比较已经表明，日本13岁学生的平均成绩更高，而英格兰低分学生所占的比例也更大。顺带一提，英格兰学生的成绩差异也大得多。
column12: attainers|n. 取得某一成绩的学生

column1: The percentage of Gross National Product spent on education is reasonably similar in the two countries, so how is this higher and more consistent attainment in maths achieved?
column2: 两国用于教育的支出占国民生产总值的比例相当接近。那么，日本的数学成绩是如何做到既更高又更稳定的呢？
column4: Gross National Product|国民生产总值

column1: Lower secondary schools in Japan cover three school years, from the seventh grade (age 13) to the ninth grade (age 15).
column2: 日本的初中学制为三年，从七年级（13岁）到九年级（15岁）。

column1: Virtually all pupils at this stage attend state schools: only 3 per cent are in the private sector.
column2: 这一阶段的学生几乎全都就读于公立学校，只有3%在私立学校就读。

column1: Schools are usually modern in design, set well back from the road and spacious inside.
column2: 校舍通常设计现代，与道路相隔一段距离，内部空间宽敞。
column6: set well back from|与……之间留有较长的距离

column1: Classrooms are large and pupils sit at single desks in rows.
column2: 教室很大，单人课桌排成一行行，学生就坐在这些课桌前。

column1: Lessons last for a standardised 50 minutes and are always followed by a 10-minute break, which gives the pupils a chance to let off steam.
column2: 每节课统一为50分钟，课后总有10分钟的休息时间，让学生有机会放松一下。
column8: let off steam|释放积压的精力或情绪

column1: Teachers begin with a formal address and mutual bowing, and then concentrate on whole-class teaching.
column2: 上课时，教师先正式致意，师生互相鞠躬，随后教师便专注于全班教学。

column1: Classes are large - usually about 40 - and are unstreamed.
column2: 班级规模很大，通常每班约40人，学生不按学业水平分班。
column6: unstreamed|adj. 不按学业水平分班的

column1: Pupils stay in the same class for all lessons throughout the school and develop considerable class identity and loyalty.
column2: 学生在校期间每门课都和同一班同学一起上，因此对班级有很强的认同感和忠诚感。

column1: Pupils attend the school in their own neighbourhood, which in theory removes ranking by school.
column2: 学生就读于所在社区的学校，理论上这消除了学校之间的高下之分。

column1: In practice in Tokyo, because of the relative concentration of schools, there is some competition to get into the ‘better’ school in a particular area.
column2: 实际情况是，东京的学校较为集中，因此同一区域里的学生要进所谓“更好的”学校，还是有一定竞争的。

column1: Traditional ways of teaching form the basis of the lesson and the remarkably quiet classes take their own notes of the points made and the examples demonstrated.
column2: 课堂教学以传统教法为基础。学生们格外安静，各自把老师讲解的要点和演示的例题记下来。
column4: form the basis of|构成……的基础
column6: take their own notes|自己记笔记

column1: Everyone has their own copy of the textbook supplied by the central education authority, Monbusho, as part of the concept of free compulsory education up to the age of 15.
column2: 每个学生都有一本由中央教育主管部门文部省提供的教科书，这体现了让学生在15岁以前接受免费义务教育的理念。
column6: central education authority|中央教育主管部门
column7: as part of|作为……的一部分
column9: free compulsory education|免费义务教育
column10: up to the age of|一直到……岁

column1: These textbooks are, on the whole, small, presumably inexpensive to produce, but well set out and logically developed.
column2: 总的来说，这些教科书小巧，制作成本想必不高，编排却很清楚，内容也循序展开。

column1: (One teacher was particularly keen to introduce colour and pictures into maths textbooks: he felt this would make them more accessible to pupils brought up in a cartoon culture.)
column2: （一位教师很希望在数学课本中加入色彩和图片。他觉得，对于在漫画文化中长大的学生，这样的课本会更容易理解。）

column1: Besides approving textbooks, Monbusho also decides the highly centralised national curriculum and how it is to be delivered.
column2: 文部省除了审定教科书，还决定高度统一的全国课程设置，以及这些课程的实施方式。

column1: Lessons all follow the same pattern.
column2: 所有课都遵循同样的模式。

column1: At the beginning, the pupils put solutions to the homework on the board, then the teachers comment, correct or elaborate as necessary.
column2: 上课伊始，学生把家庭作业的解答写在黑板上，然后教师加以点评，按需要纠正或进一步说明。

column1: Pupils mark their own homework: this is an important principle in Japanese schooling as it enables pupils to see where and why they made a mistake, so that these can be avoided in future.
column2: 学生自己批改作业。这是日本学校教育的一条重要原则，因为这样学生能看清自己错在哪里、为什么出错，今后就可以避免再犯。

column1: No one minds mistakes or ignorance as long as you are prepared to learn from them.
column2: 只要你愿意从中学习，就没有人介意你犯错或有所不知。

column1: After the homework has been discussed, the teacher explains the topic of the lesson, slowly and with a lot of repetition and elaboration.
column2: 讨论完作业后，老师慢慢讲解这节课的主题，反复说明，并作详细阐释。

column1: Examples are demonstrated on the board; questions from the textbook are worked through first with the class, and then the class is set questions from the textbook to do individually.
column2: 老师在黑板上演示例题，先和全班一起逐步解答课本上的题目，再布置课本习题，让学生独立完成。

column1: Only rarely are supplementary worksheets distributed in a maths class.
column2: 数学课上很少发补充练习单。

column1: The impression is that the logical nature of the textbooks and their comprehensive coverage of different types of examples, combined with the relative homogeneity of the class, renders work sheets unnecessary.
column2: 给人的印象是，教科书条理清晰，各类例题覆盖全面，再加上班上学生的水平比较接近，练习单也就没有必要了。

column1: At this point, the teacher would circulate and make sure that all the pupils were coping well.
column2: 这时，教师会在教室里巡视，看看是否每个学生都能顺利做下去。

column1: It is remarkable that large, mixed-ability classes could be kept together for maths throughout all their compulsory schooling from 6 to 15.
column2: 从6岁到15岁，整个义务教育阶段，不同水平的学生竟然都能一直留在同一个大班里上数学课，这一点很不寻常。
column4: mixed-ability classes|不同水平学生混编的班级

column1: Teachers say that they give individual help at the end of a lesson or after school, setting extra work if necessary.
column2: 教师们说，他们会在一节课结束时或放学后给学生个别辅导，必要时再布置额外的作业。
column4: at the end of|在……结束时
column6: setting extra work|布置额外作业

column1: In observed lessons, any strugglers would be assisted by the teacher or quietly seek help from their neighbour.
column2: 在所观察的课堂上，学习有困难的学生会得到老师的帮助，或者小声向邻座同学求助。
column4: strugglers|n. 学习有困难的学生

column1: Carefully fostered class identity makes pupils keen to help each other - anyway, it is in their interests since the class progresses together.
column2: 精心培养起来的班级认同感使学生乐于互相帮助。况且，这也符合他们自己的利益，因为全班是一起往前学的。
column8: in their interests|符合他们的利益

column1: This scarcely seems adequate help to enable slow learners to keep up.
column2: 这样的帮助似乎还远不足以让学得慢的学生跟上进度。

column1: However, the Japanese attitude towards education runs along the lines of ‘if you work hard enough, you can do almost anything’.
column2: 不过，日本人对教育的看法大致是：“只要你足够努力，几乎什么都能做到。”
column5: runs along the lines of|大致是这样的

column1: Parents are kept closely informed of their children’s progress and will play a part in helping their children to keep up with class, sending them to ‘Juku’ (private evening tuition) if extra help is needed and encouraging them to work harder.
column2: 家长能及时、详细地了解孩子的学习进展，也会帮助孩子跟上全班的进度。如果孩子需要额外帮助，家长会送他们去“塾”（私立夜间补习班），并鼓励他们更加努力。
column3: kept closely informed of|随时向……详细通报
column5: play a part in|参与；发挥作用
column7: private evening tuition|私立夜间补习

column1: It seems to work, at least for 95 per cent of the school population.
column2: 这种做法似乎有效，至少对95%的在校学生是如此。

column1: So what are the major contributing factors in the success of maths teaching?
column2: 那么，数学教学之所以成功，主要有哪些促成因素呢？

column1: Clearly, attitudes are important.
column2: 显然，态度很重要。

column1: Education is valued greatly in Japanese culture; maths is recognised as an important compulsory subject throughout schooling; and the emphasis is on hard work coupled with a focus on accuracy.
column2: 日本文化十分重视教育。学生在校期间，数学始终被视为一门重要的必修课；教学既强调勤奋，也注重准确。
column8: throughout schooling|在整个学校教育阶段

column1: Other relevant points relate to the supportive attitude of a class towards slower pupils, the lack of competition within a class, and the positive emphasis on learning for oneself and improving one’s own standard.
column2: 其他相关因素还包括，全班同学对学习进度较慢的学生持支持态度，班内缺少竞争，而且班级积极鼓励学生自主学习、提高自己的水平。

column1: And the view of repetitively boring lessons and learning the facts by heart, which is sometimes quoted in relation to Japanese classes, may be unfair and unjustified.
column2: 有时人们谈及日本课堂，会说课上反复做同样的事、枯燥乏味，只要求把事实背下来。这样的看法也许有失公允，缺乏依据。

column1: No poor maths lessons were observed.
column2: 在观察到的数学课中，没有一节上得差。

column1: They were mainly good and one or two were inspirational.
column2: 大多数课上得很好，还有一两节很能启发人。
